info.title: CF Meet Notification Service internal API
info.description: Internal signed API of the unified Notification Service (cfmeet.notifications; blueprint Document 4 §3.3): I1–I11, the optional I12 (approved under D-15) and I13 (roadmap N9, the Messaging push-registration facade and D-1b copy) and I3c (1.3.0, gap audit C1: the cancellation of a call ring). Frozen by roadmap N1 before the service exists (lifecycle experimental). Every route except I12 requires a packages/service-auth token whose issuer holds the stated permission in the receiver's trust bundle (x-cfmeet-internal-permission); durable jti nonces; request binding emitted from day one. Never routed by public ingress. Health (/health, /ready with routingProtocol and per-lane heartbeats) is not counted as an API. 1.4.0 (ADR 0063 partner push, phase B5; all of it only while NOTIFICATIONS_PARTNER_PUSH_ENABLED is on, default off: the provider routes answer 404 and the partner shapes are refused exactly as before): N-P1 the push provider vault under /internal/v1/push/providers/{tenantId}/{applicationId}/{environmentId}[/{provider}[/verify]] (notifications-push-provider.manage, Developer Console only; the credential arrives sealed with packages/notification-client seal_push_credential for exactly that scope, is stored sealed under the service's data keys, and is never returned or logged); N-P2 I13 also accepts platform-principal subjects (APNS / APNS_VOIP / FCM, keyed by scope, principal, installation and platform); N-P3 I3 also accepts a platform-principal recipient (APNS_VOIP PushKit pushes on topic <bundleId>.voip, FCM high-priority data messages, with that scope's own credential only; recipientStatus); N-P4 platform-principal:<environmentId>:<principalId> recipients of messaging.message.created (cfmeet.notifications.event 1.5.0) are delivered with the partner's credential; N-P5 per-scope counters notif_partner_push_sent_total / notif_partner_push_failed_total{environment,lane,platform[,class]}. 1.5.0 (ADR 0067, admin bridge): operator attribution (X-CF-Operator, X-CF-Approver, X-CF-Approval-Ref, X-CF-Intent-Digest) accepted only from cfmeet.admin-bridge and refused on every route from any other caller (403 FORBIDDEN); the admin bridge's operator reads GET /internal/v1/operator/deliveries and /failed-deliveries (time window, newest first), /email-suppressions (by address or digest; keyed digest only) and /providers (status only, never credentials), each requiring notifications.administer and X-CF-Operator.

post.description: Batch of ≤ 100 cfmeet.notifications.event envelopes from the caller's own outbox. producer must equal the token issuer; per-producer closed type allowlist; dedupe by (producer, eventId) plus request digest; route.decisionId unique per producer; a route that is not NEW is REJECTED; an event for a category whose service mode is not ACTIVE/SHADOW is HELD (stored, never sent, alert raised), never dropped. ACCEPTED only after commit (the responsibility boundary, §9.5); DUPLICATE has ACCEPTED semantics. 503 + Retry-After under STANDARD backpressure; CRITICAL is never refused. Unsupported route.protocol → 503 PROTOCOL_UNSUPPORTED (another replica may accept).

dryRun.description: Probe only (§9.5): reports whether each eventId was committed (DUPLICATE) or not (UNKNOWN); writes nothing.

shadow.description: 1.1.0 (N3): the batch holds producer SHADOW copies of OLD decisions (routing mode SHADOW). They are recorded and evaluated for the shadow comparison and are never delivered, whatever the service-side mode, so a mode disagreement can never turn a shadow copy into a second delivery.

200.description: Per-event outcomes (always 200 for a well-formed batch).

reason.description: For REJECTED / HELD: a machine reason (e.g. ROUTE_NOT_NEW, TYPE_NOT_ALLOWED, PRODUCER_MISMATCH, DIGEST_MISMATCH, CATEGORY_NOT_ACTIVE).

post.description: Synchronous, ≤ 1 s, no queue, no retry (the WebSocket ring and the recovery API cover failure). Called post-commit, best-effort, by Calling; ringing and first-answer arbitration stay in Calling. APNs VoIP / FCM high priority / Web Push urgency high. 1.2.0 (N9): the TTL is what is left of the invitation (expiresAt, at most 300 s), call alerts collapse (Web Push Topic / apns-collapse-id / FCM collapse_key cfmeet-call), APNS_VOIP endpoints receive a PushKit VoIP push; the device payload is the metadata {v, type: call} only. 1.3.0 (gap audit S15): when recipientAccountRef is present, the account's incomingCalls preference (the Hub switch copied by N10) and the push channel of INCOMING_CALLS apply; off answers PREFERENCE_OFF and nothing is sent. 1.4.0 (ADR 0063 N-P3, only while NOTIFICATIONS_PARTNER_PUSH_ENABLED is on): the body may instead name a platform-principal recipient {kind, tenantId, applicationId, environmentId, principalId}; pushTargetRefs is then optional (default: every APNS_VOIP and FCM installation of that principal; references of anything else answer UNKNOWN_TARGET). APNS_VOIP installations get a PushKit VoIP push (apns-push-type voip, topic <bundleId>.voip), FCM installations a high-priority data message, each with that scope's own credential only (never CF Meet's); same rules as today: synchronous, ≤ 1 s, no retry, metadata {v, type: call} only. Gated by the flag alone (the first-party CALL_INVITATIONS routing mode does not apply). recipientStatus: SENT (at least one installation), NO_REGISTRATION, NO_CREDENTIAL (the scope has no credential for its installations' platforms: nothing is sent), FAILED or EXPIRED.

recipientAccountRef.description: 1.2.0 (N9): the invited CF Meet account. When present, only push endpoints of this account are woken; a pushTargetRef of another account answers UNKNOWN_TARGET. Calling sends it for first-party (FIRST_PARTY tenant, NATIVE_CF_USER cfmeet-user:) recipients only.

post.description: 1.3.0 (gap audit C1). Called post-commit, best-effort, by Calling when a ringing invitation of a first-party recipient ends without being answered on that endpoint: answered elsewhere, cancelled by the caller, expired, or the Call ended. Same permission and bounds as I3 (synchronous, ≤ 1 s, no queue, no retry; off unless CALL_INVITATIONS is ACTIVE: NOT_CONFIGURED). The device payload is the metadata {v, type: call-cancel} only, sent with the ring's collapse id (cfmeet-call: a ring still waiting at the provider is replaced, so the device never rings) and a 60 s TTL. Never a PushKit VoIP push: APNS_VOIP endpoints answer SKIPPED_VOIP (the app ends its CallKit call from signaling / recovery). Only the recipient account's endpoints are reached (another account's pushTargetRef answers UNKNOWN_TARGET); the incomingCalls preference applies as for I3 (PREFERENCE_OFF: no ring was sent). No call id, number, name or other call detail is accepted.

recipientAccountRef.description: The invited CF Meet account (cfmeet-user:<uuid>). Required: only this account's endpoints are reached.

post.description: Roadmap N9, D-1b copy path. Messaging mirrors the push registrations of CF Meet first-party accounts (ACTIVE NATIVE_CF_USER principals of the CF Meet personal scope whose Platform Access reference is cfmeet-user:<uuid>) into the service's push endpoints: the one-off copy and every later change through its registration facade. Idempotent per item (UNCHANGED when already mirrored); each item is its own transaction. The endpoint is keyed by Messaging's scope and device and owned by accountRef, so MESSAGE_WAKEUPS deliveries resolve it. An account-device registration (U8) of the same handle is authoritative (SUPERSEDED / HANDLE_IN_USE, the copy is not kept). When the service has the CF Meet first-party scope configured, other scopes answer OUT_OF_SCOPE. Handles are checked as at U8 (including the Web Push host allowlist), sealed at rest, never echoed or logged. 1.3.0 (ADR 0063 N-P2, only while NOTIFICATIONS_PARTNER_PUSH_ENABLED is on): an item may instead carry a platform-principal subject, either nested {subject: {kind, tenantId, applicationId, environmentId, principalId, installationId}, platform, handle?, enabled?} or flat {kind, tenantId, …, installationId, platform, handle?, enabled?}, with platform APNS, APNS_VOIP or FCM. The endpoint is keyed by (scope, principal, installation, platform), owned by no CF Meet account, its handle checked structurally, sealed and digested in its environment's own domain. enabled defaults to the presence of handle; enabled false removes the installation's endpoint of that platform (or, without platform, all of them). First-party items of the same batch are applied exactly as before. Invalid partner items answer INVALID with reason SUBJECT, SCOPE (the CF Meet first-party scope), INSTALLATION, PLATFORM or HANDLE.

post.description: D-15 (approved): operator alert delivery through the service. Alertmanager cannot sign service tokens, so this route takes a static bearer file held by Alertmanager, on a private listener reachable only from the monitoring network; each alert becomes an operator.alert.fired event (producer alertmanager) to the configured operator group. The service's OWN health alerts never depend on this route: they use an independent receiver path.

put.summary: Store a sealed partner push credential (N-P1)
put.description: ADR 0063 N-P1. Opens the seal for exactly this (tenant, application, environment), checks the fingerprint, metadata and key (an APNs .p8 PKCS#8 P-256 key; an FCM service-account key), and stores it sealed under the service data keys bound to this scope and provider; a replaced credential returns to UNVERIFIED. An environment holds one credential per provider for one (tenant, application) only: a credential of the same environment under another tenant or application answers 409 VERSION_CONFLICT. The credential only ever sends to endpoints of the same scope.

sealed.description: The secret (the APNs .p8 PEM, or the FCM service-account JSON) sealed to the service with packages/notification-client, in one of two forms. (1) Whole: seal::seal_push_credential(key, tenantId, applicationId, environmentId, secret) — HPKE base mode, info cfmeet.notifications.push-provider.v1, AAD cfmeet.push-provider|<tenantId>|<applicationId>|<environmentId> — sent as the compact string <kid>.<enc>.<ct> (Sealed::to_compact), the object {kid, enc, ct}, or that object JSON-encoded. (2) Parts (what the Developer Console sends): {"v":1,"parts":[{kid,enc,ct},…]} (object or JSON-encoded string, 1–64 parts): the secret's base64url (no padding) split into ≤ 512-character token parts, each sealed with seal::seal for producer cfmeet.developer-platform, event id <tenantId>/<applicationId>/<environmentId>/<provider> and event type push-provider.secret.<index>-of-<count>. Either form opens only for this scope (and, for parts, this provider slot and part order); anything else is 400 VALIDATION_ERROR.

metadata.description: Non-secret facts. APNS / APNS_VOIP: teamId and keyId (10 letters or digits), bundleId (the app bundle id; a trailing .voip is removed, the VoIP topic <bundleId>.voip is derived) and apnsHost are required, projectId is refused. FCM: only projectId (optional; must equal the service account project_id, filled from it when absent).

post.summary: Verify a partner push credential with its provider (N-P1)
post.description: ADR 0063 N-P1. APNs: signs a provider JWT (ES256) from the .p8 and presents it with a placeholder device token (Apple authenticates the token and refuses the placeholder: VERIFIED). FCM: obtains an OAuth access token from the service account and addresses a placeholder registration token. Nothing reaches a device. A provider that cannot be reached keeps the stored status and answers lastError PROVIDER_UNAVAILABLE.
